html:
SMTO-MEM-0002 — The memory list lost its place

GUID: eb63b150-6cf2-44f3-aeaf-ff88691d3461
Slug: memory-invalid-cursor
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • The Agent asked Memory for the next page of a list, but the bookmark it used was damaged or came from a different list. No memories were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list your memories again from the beginning, using the same filter as before. A fresh list gives the Agent a new, valid bookmark for later pages.
  2. If you need to browse many memories yourself, open Memory Editor and use its search and tag filter. Memory Editor keeps its own place in the list, so you can browse without relying on the Agent's bookmark.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's memory list returns entries and continues to later pages without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which filter the Agent used. Don't delete memories to fix this; your saved memories are unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Memory rejected a memory.list request because its continuation cursor could not be decoded or did not belong to the requested listing (different version, prefix, tag or key position).

What this means

  • Memory enumeration cannot decode its cursor or the decoded version, prefix or after-key does not belong to the requested listing. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • Memory enumeration cannot decode its cursor or the decoded version, prefix or after-key does not belong to the requested listing.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact prefix and current returned cursor instead of fabricating an offset.

How to fix it

  • The memory.list cursor could not be decoded, was over 1024 characters, or its version, prefix, tag or after-key did not match the current request. Start the listing again without a cursor and pass only the next cursor returned with the same prefix and tag.
  • Restart enumeration or query from the first page and use the new returned cursor.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh enumeration and its returned continuation cover the intended prefix.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
